signals.title: USD/JPY — Geopolitical Risk + Crowded Carry
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.27, holding just below the SMA20 at 159.19 while maintaining a significant 275bp Fed-BoJ OIS carry advantage. Headlines confirm the US Navy has cleared the Strait of Hormuz of mines, but US sanctions on Iran keep the geopolitical risk premium active. Despite the underlying carry support, the options market is pricing in heavy downside protection with a strong 25d risk reversal of -1.86, while the spot-VIX correlation has flipped to +0.433 (z=+2.10σ), indicating JPY has lost its typical safe-haven function. Speculative positioning remains net short JPY at -73,641, though recent flow shows a WoW delta of -14,115, suggesting the short is being trimmed as intervention risk looms near the 160.00 handle. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry dominance persists while price holds above SMA200 at 158.34. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias 1.0% priced. Risk: Sustained break above 160.00 triggers confirmed BoJ/MoF intervention, forcing a disorderly unwind of crowded shorts.

signals.title: AUD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: AUD/CHF emerges as the dominant G10 trend this week as the AUD 1W average hits +0.712% while CHF lags at -0.456%, creating a 1.168% bilateral spread. The divergence is fundamentally anchored by a massive 435bp carry premium (RBA 4.35% vs SNB 0.0%), rewarding AUD longs in the current normal volatility regime (VIX 15.7). Technicals reinforce the move as AUD/USD remains positioned above its SMA20/50/200 cluster, though the ESI at -8.5 warns of moderate data disappointment. Retail sentiment is extremely short AUD/CHF at 86%, providing a contrarian tailwind as retail traders attempt to fade the institutional carry trend. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/CHF; carry-seeking flows capitalize on the CHF weakness. Catalyst: SEK rate decision 25 Aug for broader G10 sentiment. Risk: VIX spike above 25 revives CHF safe-haven demand and compresses the carry advantage.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Extreme + Vol Premium
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1674, maintaining its position above the SMA200 at 1.1635 despite Scotiabank reporting limited upside above fair value. Speculative positioning is currently at a 52-week extreme with a pctl(52w) of 10 and z-score of -1.99, showing a crowded net short of -76,035 contracts. The options market is demanding a high premium for protection, with ATM IV at 7.1% vs HV30 of 4.5%, creating a +2.6% vol risk premium. This combination of extreme positioning and elevated VRP suggests the market is heavily hedged against a short-squeeze rather than chasing new lows. Trade bias: Neutral/range EUR/USD; crowded positioning and high vol premium limit immediate directional conviction. Catalyst: ECB meeting 10 Sep — hike bias 2.4% priced. Risk: Resilience in German Ifo data triggers a short-covering rally toward 1.1800.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Carry Neutral + Options Complacency
signals.text: GBP/USD is holding at 1.3635, supported by its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster (SMA20 at 1.3502). The Fed-BoE carry spread is currently neutral at 0bp, leaving the pair reliant on relative data performance and risk appetite rather than carry-seeking flows. While COT positioning is reaching the upper decile (pctl 94, z +1.45), the 25d risk reversal is near neutral at -0.09, showing no urgent demand for downside protection. The ESI of -8.3 reflects moderate negative bias in UK data, which is likely to cap further upside despite the bullish technical alignment. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; technical trend remains intact while SMA200 at 1.3429 holds. Catalyst: US CPI next week. Risk: LF net long of +46,070 triggers a profit-taking reversal if US yields rebound sharply.
